Instrument: Zhang & Lu (2010), Adolescents' Emotional Resilience Questionnaire.
note: Clean gate pass (validate_items.R --table-sets: 11 items ERQ_1..ERQ_11 exact; resp set 1-6 exact); 66 rows (11 items x 6 levels), n=1087 per item. CODE DERIVATION: positional -- data/gao_2022_covid_stress.py assigns ERQ_{i+1} to raw.iloc[:, 66+i] after asserting column 66 contains the marker 问卷四. Each header cell is the full Chinese stem prefixed with its own number '1.'..'11.', and the numbers run 1..11 across columns 66..76, so position and printed number agree. MAPPING (data_labels, but Step 5b still owed because the derivation is positional): header diff 11/11 -- shipped item_text for ERQ_k is byte-identical to the header at column 65+k with the leading 'k.' stripped; and a respondent-level join on 序号 shows live ERQ_k equals raw column 65+k for 1087/1087 respondents (diagonal 1.000) while every other column agrees at most 0.651. Per-item level counts also match cell for cell (e.g. ERQ_1 68/71/134/301/311/202, ERQ_11 96/104/197/367/206/117). TRANSCRIPTION: item_text = the header stems verbatim (full-width punctuation and the curly quotes around 自我找乐 in item 8 kept). instructions = the 问卷四 block instruction carried in column 66's header ('以下描述的是...进行选择：'), with the questionnaire label '问卷四' and the '—' separator before item 1 dropped. instrument is an IRW-written name (the file calls the block only 问卷四). language=Chinese. TRANSLATION: no English wording exists in the deposit or the paper (the paper names the ERQ and describes it but quotes no item), so all _translated fields are this project's own translation from the Chinese (translation_source=machine_translation) -- an issues-page line is owed once the table is live. OPTIONS NOT SHIPPED: option_text blank for resp 1-6. The xlsx stores bare integers with no value labels, and the paper says items are 'rated from 0 (never) to 6 (always)' -- seven points -- whereas the data carry six levels 1-6 for every item (no 0, no 7); a 6-point agreement scale is what the stored codes suggest, but no source ties an anchor to a stored code, so none is padded or guessed. POLARITY CAVEAT (data, not text): the negatively worded items 2,5,7,10,11 form their own correlation block (within r .48-.67) and correlate ~0 with the positive items 1,3,4,6,8,9 (-.10 to +.21) -- the content split corroborates the mapping, but whether the negative items are stored raw or reversed cannot be settled: alpha is .81 raw and .80 with them reversed, against a published .845 on the paper's 873-case analysis subset (the IRW table keeps all 1087 submissions). STEP 3b: matches -- 11 items, 6-level scale, the fourth questionnaire block, ERQ as named in the paper and dictionary. RIGHTS: silence. The wording is the originators' own (Zhang & Lu 2010, a Chinese journal with no licence terms found); IRW's copy comes from the study's CC BY 4.0 PLOS deposit; instrument_rights_register.csv has no ERQ/Zhang-Lu row; no fee, permission, NC, ND or redistribution clause located. No register row written (a round may not write ship rows). No new irw_fetch export: the gate ran with --table-sets; the per-respondent checks used the local irw cache populated by table_context.R.
public_note: Item and instruction text is the administered Chinese from the study's data file, with English translations produced by IRW; response options are unlabelled because the paper describes a 0-6 never-to-always scale while the data hold six levels (1-6).

Bowling OPQOL-brief form, https://ilcuk.org.uk/wp-content/uploads/2019/03/OPQOL-brief-questionnaire-and-responses.pdf (sha256 693e0239affb8131...), items 1-13; mapping check: Buzgova, Kozakova, Zelenikova, Bobcikova (2022) BMC Geriatrics 22:534, PMC9219227, doi:10.1186/s12877-022-03198-x, Table 2 (Europe PMC fullTextXML sha256 17380d4b1ce7ec79...); study: Buzgova et al. (2023) PLOS ONE doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0283772 (JATS sha256 182332ddf54b7ff2...), S1 File .s001 (.sav, no labels, sha256 3bce1db706ce009e...); data/buzgova_2023_elder_battery.py
note: Code derivation: item IS the source .sav column name (data/buzgova_2023_elder_battery.py melts [f'QoL{i}' for i in 1..13] unrenamed) -- not positional. The .sav carries NO variable labels and NO value labels on any column (pyreadstat: 0 variable labels, 0 value-label sets), and the PLOS paper names the OPQOL-brief (Bowling et al. 2013, ref 32; '13 statements', total 13-65) but reproduces no items, so no level-1 or level-2 source ties codes to text. Mapping QoL<n> -> OPQOL-brief item <n> is therefore paper_order (the form's own numbering), then VERIFIED against Table 2 of the same group's Czech OPQOL-brief validation (PMC9219227, n=954, overlapping Moravian-Silesian sample), which prints per-item Mean/SD/corrected item-total r against English item wording i1-I13: after reversing live resp (6-resp) all 13 means agree within 0.028, SDs within 0.019, item-total r within 0.014, total 54.32/6.79 vs published 54.49/6.83; a Hungarian assignment over all three statistics returns the identity and every one of the 78 pairwise swaps is worse (tightest: 3<->7, the two health items, penalty 21.2 vs identity cost 13.9); QoL3-QoL7 is also the strongest inter-item r (0.705), as the two 'healthy enough to...' items should be. See verify_buzgova_2023_qol.R. Step 3b: 13 items, resp 1-5 with all five levels used by every item (966-983 rows/item) = OPQOL-brief shape; no mismatch. The preliminary single global-QoL item on the form is not an OPQOL-brief item and is not in the table (the .sav's separate kz1 column was not checked against it and is not part of this table). Response direction: live resp is stored RAW on the form's own coding (1=Strongly agree ... 5=Strongly disagree); all 13 items are positively worded, so low resp = better QoL. Evidence: raw item means 1.63-2.10; total correlates Spearman +0.60 with the LSITA-SF12 total (higher = worse satisfaction; paper reports r=0.592), +0.53 with GDS-15, -0.43 with RSES. Nothing is stored reverse-scored, so anchors are the same for every item and are NOT flipped. Note the PLOS paper's Methods say 'higher scores indicating better QoL', which is true of the reversed Bowling scoring but not of the released columns or of the paper's own reported correlations. Language: administered in Czech (the group's own translation, per PMC9219227 Methods: two forward translations, back-translation, cognitive debriefing). No Czech wording exists in the .sav (no labels), the PLOS paper, its S1 file, or PMC9219227 (full text has Czech only in reference titles; its Europe PMC supplementaryFiles bundle holds only Fig 1). Fallback taken: canonical English in the base fields, language=Czech, _translated columns empty, translation_source=official_instrument_english. Transcription: items verbatim from the Bowling form incl. UK spelling 'neighbours' and 'I can please myself what I do' (PMC9219227 prints variant English: 'neighbors', 'I can please myself in what I do', 'hobbies I enjoy doing' -- not used). Instructions are the form's row instruction ('Please tick one box in each row...'); the form's lead-in 'We would like to ask you about your quality of life:' belongs to the unscored global item and was dropped. Option label 'Neither agree nor disagree' is the form's column header (its scoring note abbreviates it to 'Neither'). Rights: express grant on the rights holder's own form -- 'OPQOL-brief: Copyrighted @ A. Bowling. This questionnaire is free to use and no permissions are needed. The request is that the source is credited: Bowling A, Hankins M, Windle G, Bilotta C, Grant R. (2013)...' (ilcuk.org.uk PDF above, sha256 693e0239affb81316905afba6ef129c8848110f2433cfd5e55f2f5a129e16127). A credit request reserves no right (no fee, permission, NC, ND or redistribution clause); credit carried in public_note. Outranks the PsycTESTS record 10.1037/t28733-000. No register row written (rounds may not write ship rows); lead from irw#2381/#2382 (OBTAINABLE).
public_note: The OPQOL-brief was administered in Czech, but the Czech wording is not published in the study's paper or data file, so the canonical English OPQOL-brief items are shown; responses are stored on the form's raw coding (1 = Strongly agree ... 5 = Strongly disagree), so for every item a lower value means better quality of life. note: Code derivation: item IS the S6 Dataset column name (the processing script melts ExpHands/ExpRobots/ExpTech/ExpProg/ExpProgRob unrenamed). CODEBOOK WORDING, NOT ADMINISTERED STEMS: the administered questionnaire wording for these five items is not published. Checked: S1 File (curriculum booklet), S1 Appendix (.s010; lists only the 7 confidence items), S2 Appendix (.s011, excluded data), S3 Appendix (.s012; names the covariates as 'experience with hands-on activities, technology, robots, computer programming, and programming robots'), the S1-S6 Dataset CSVs (bare column headers), and the article text. The only code-to-text tie is the S2 File codebook, which describes each column in third person, e.g. 'ExpRobots: Participants' level of experience with robots reported on a scale from 1 -5 (1: no experience, 5: lots of experience)'. SKILL.md/itemtext_standard.md do not forbid descriptive codebook text (the standard defines item_text as the literal prompt; the closest rulings are 'use terse labels for the mapping and the best available text for the words, and record the swap' and the #1770 referent test, which this passes). The codebook is the best available, study-authored text, so it ships, disclosed here and in public_note, rather than being upgraded to an invented first-person stem. Deviations: item_text is the codebook description with its trailing scale clause (' reported on a scale from 1 -5 (1: no experience, 5: lots of experience)') removed and moved to option_text/resp; everything before it is verbatim incl. the curly apostrophe and '(example: woodworking, crafting)'. option_text resp=1 'No experience' and resp=5 'Lots of experience' use the capitalisation the article quotes (the S2 File has them lower-case); resp 2-4 unlabelled in every source, left blank. instructions blank (none published). mapping_basis=paper_explicit: the tie is a supplement (not the data file) listing the live codes against descriptions. Step 5b VERIFIED: the article's Participants section reports M/SD for four of the five (robots 2.41/1.12, technology 4.15/0.82, programming 3.96/0.94, programming robots 2.30/1.27); live values 2.407/1.118, 4.148/0.818, 3.963/0.940, 2.296/1.265 match each claimed code and no other; ExpHands (3.111, unpublished) by elimination and its self-describing name. Rights: study-authored items (no source instrument cited), CC BY 4.0 article; no restriction to quote. Language: English (US university study; no other language mentioned). Data: N=27 per item, matching the paper's analysed sample (28 recruited, 1 dropped).
public_note: Item text is the study's own codebook description of each experience rating (e.g. "Participants' level of experience with robots"), not the question wording participants read, which was not published; only the endpoints 1 and 5 of the scale are labelled.
